post_text:
I almost killed an engineer's best idea because it did not match the picture in my head.

During a heated review three years ago, I held the whiteboard marker like a shield.

She proposed a direction that contradicted how I had solved similar challenges for a decade. My immediate instinct was to pull rank and steer the room back toward familiar ground.

Instead, I saw the quiet conviction in her notes and decided to bite my tongue.

I handed her the project and let her run with it entirely. Over the next month, she built something simpler and far more elegant than the convoluted plan I had championed.

She proved that my years of pattern-matching had quietly turned into an invisible blind spot.

Giving away true ownership means accepting that someone might solve the puzzle differently than you would.

It requires stepping back from the steering wheel and trusting someone else to succeed on their own terms.

Sometimes the hardest work you will ever do is simply stepping out of the way. 🤝
lesson_extracted: Seniority is about creating space for others to succeed on their own terms, even when their solution challenges your instincts.
